name: SSHI_FBR
rationale: The reference FBR fails because the piezo open-circuit voltage amplitude (~0.76V) is too low to overcome diode drops and reach the 1.8V target. I am implementing a Parallel-SSHI (Synchronized Switch Harvesting on Inductor) topology. By using an inductor L1 and a switch S1 to flip the piezoelectric capacitance charge at the voltage extrema, we can effectively increase the voltage available to the rectifier, allowing Vout to reach and sustain levels between 1.8V and 3.6V. A full-bridge rectifier (FBR) is used to harvest energy from both half-cycles, and a DZ33 zener diode clamps the output to prevent exceeding the 3.6V absolute maximum during strong excitation (S3).

name: SSHI_HalfBridge
rationale: This is a simplified version of the SSHI converter that grounds pzn to reduce the number of diode drops in the rectification path. While the piezo is a floating current source, grounding one terminal allows for a half-bridge rectifier (single diode), which reduces the total forward voltage drop from ~0.5V (two DSCH diodes) to ~0.25V. This may improve startup time and Vavg under the weakest excitation conditions (S4).

name: SECE_Basic
rationale: Implementing a basic Synchronized Electric Charge Extraction (SECE) circuit. Instead of an inductor to flip the voltage, SECE uses an external capacitor to temporarily store the piezo charge and then discharge it into the output capacitor. This is another proven method to boost the harvested voltage of piezo transducers beyond the open-circuit limit without requiring the precise L-Cp resonance timing of SSHI.
